```plato
    // The body after an impulse of `impulse` newton-seconds applied at world point
    // `point`. Position and orientation are untouched: an impulse changes velocity
    // only, and an immovable body changes not at all.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impulse_(physics))
    ApplyImpulse(self: SolverBody3D, impulse: Vector3D, point: Point3D): SolverBody3D
        => SolverBody3D(
            self.Center,
            self.Orientation,
            SpatialVelocity3D(
                self.Velocity.Linear + impulse * self.InverseMass,
                self.Velocity.Angular
                    + AngularResponse(self, self.Center.Between(point).Cross(impulse))),
            self.InverseMass,
            self.InverseInertia,
            self.LinearDamping,
            self.AngularDamping,
            self.GravityScale);
```

## Line 506

**Source:** [stdlib/future/rigid-dynamics.library.plato, line 506](../../../../../stdlib/future/rigid-dynamics.library.plato#L506).

```plato

    // The body after an explosion: an impulse directed away from the blast centre,
    // at full magnitude at the centre and falling linearly to nothing at the
    // radius, applied at the body's own centre so that it pushes without spinning.
    // A body outside the radius, or exactly at the centre, is untouched.
    ApplyImpulse(self: SolverBody3D, blast: RadialImpulse3D): SolverBody3D
    {
        var away = blast.Center.Between(self.Center);
        var distance = away.Magnitude;
        var falloff = (1.0 - distance / blast.Radius.Amount).Clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        return distance <= 0.0
            ? self
            : ApplyImpulse(self, away / distance * (blast.Magnitude.Amount * falloff), self.Center);
    }
```
